To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CO2 binding with the cation is end-on and that the n + 1 and n + 0 structures coexist in [Cu(CO)3n]+ and [Ag(CO)3,4,5,6]+, respectively.
the CO2 binding to copper and silver cation occurs via a charge-quadupole electrostatic interactions in an end-on geometry.

the reaction of Cu+ and Ag + with CO2 leads to the formation of [M(CO 2)n]+ clusters, where the metal atom is bound to an oxygen atom in an end-on geometry, and that the n + 1 and (n -1) + 2 configurations are preferred for the interaction of Cu+ and CO2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reaction of copper and argon cations with carbon monoxide.
the reactions of carbon dioxide with cations of copper and silver.
the reactions between metal cations and carbon dioxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CO2 interacts with Cu+ and Cu+ via charge-quadrupolar electrostatic interaction, and the n + 1 structure is favored for n = 3, 4, 5, 6, while the n + 2 structure is preferred for n = 7 and 8.
CO2 binds end on to Cu+ and Ag+, and the formation of oxide-carbonate structures does not occur.
the interaction between Cu+ and CO2 is stronger than that between Ag+ and CO2, and the n + 1 structure is favored for n = 3-6 in the [Cu(CO)2n]+ complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CO2 reduction on the transition metal atoms is not as straightforward as it was thought, and that a careful consideration of the reaction mechanisms should be taken into account in the rational design of the catalysts.
CO2 is more strongly bonded to the neutral metal atoms and the metal cations than to the metal anions, which is consistent with the electronegativity order of CO2 and the metals.
the reaction of CO2 and Cu+ or Ag+ is dominated by the end-on configuration, while the side-on and bent configurations are preferred for the neutral and anion metal species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cationic transition metal atoms are not good candidates for catalyzing CO2 reduction.
the CO2 reduction activity of the metal atom depends strongly on its charge and that the cations are the most promising candidates for catalyzing the reduction of CO2.
the cationic transition metals can be used as catalysts for CO reduction to carbon monoxide.
